plain: To calm or quiet someone, often by giving in to what they want.

webster.text: To make quiet; to calm; to reduce to a state of peace; to still; to pacify; as, to appease the tumult of the ocean, or of the passions; to appease hunger or thirst.

example.quote: and informs us, at the same time, of the vast influence of that institution in appeasing the disorders and establishing the tranquillity of the empire.
